source_text.body:
Manage a Proxmox homelab with Grok Bot
A user runs Grok Bot in an Ubuntu VM on Proxmox to handle repetitive homelab management, stepping in on judgment calls or breakages, with multiple agents as fallback.
·
Nov 7, 2025
Done with
GB
Grok Bot
What they did
The user set up a small guest VM on a Proxmox test server and gave Grok SSH access plus a Cloudflare tunnel. Grok then built a server-side "submind" of scripts and services for repetitive checks and bulk tasks, kept extending it for new projects, and also built a display interface; the user mainly supplied the server, described goals, and decided permissions and when to step in for judgment calls or breakages.
How it went
It took over routine homelab work that had been consuming Grok usage just to confirm nothing changed, and surfaced issues on a rotating status screen. The post gives no hard performance numbers, only that the user still intervenes for new tasks, failures, and access decisions.
Worth knowing
The main catch is governance: the user says they still control what access the bot gets and what it is allowed to do.
Try it yourself
with
Grok Bot
Copy prompt
You're running in a VM on my Proxmox homelab. Handle these repetitive jobs: [e.g. check VM health, apply updates, review backups, restart failed services], and log what you did to [file or channel]. If something breaks or a judgment call is needed, stop and describe the problem and your options. Pause and show me the plan before deleting any VM, snapshot, or data, or changing network settings.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GrokBot/comments/1xpyfog/well_im_both_pleasantly_surprised_and_a_little
